00.what_is_already_done: Prior work predicts plant traits from images or omics and separately performs species recognition, but none ablates species identity to quantify how much apparent trait signal is species-identity-mediated.
00.remaining_novel_angle: The species-identity ablation design—comparing trait regression, label-free species-class-to-mean-trait transfer, and adversarial species-identity removal across seen/unseen species with a species-mean oracle variance decomposition—is a distinct diagnostic not addressed by the retrieved hits.

01.what_is_already_done: CNN prediction of plant functional traits from iNaturalist photos coupled with TRY data has been demonstrated, with claims of cross-taxa generalisation, and multimodal uncertainty-aware trait inference is being pursued in PlantTraitNet.
01.remaining_novel_angle: The specific contribution is a phylogenetically blocked (leave-one-family-out / leave-one-order-out) evaluation protocol that quantifies the optimism of random splits and tests whether phylogeny-aware contrastive augmentation recovers generalisation to unseen clades.

02.what_is_already_done: Prior work predicts intraspecific trait variation spatially (e.g., California grasses) and estimates individual-level plant traits at scale, while CNN+TRY studies predict species-level traits from images.
02.remaining_novel_angle: Framing a formal identifiability/prediction-ceiling result—that species-mean labels cannot yield positive within-species deviation R² regardless of model capacity—and testing a variance-aware loss against this ceiling is not addressed by the retrieved hits.

03.what_is_already_done: Self-supervised contrastive and masked-autoencoder pretraining have been benchmarked for image-based plant phenotyping and hyperspectral trait prediction, and MAE has been applied to plant variety classification, but not as a controlled head-to-head of contrastive vs regression vs reconstruction objectives on the same trait task with seen/unseen species splits.
03.remaining_novel_angle: The specific objective-identifiability comparison—contrastive vs supervised regression vs MAE vs species classification, evaluated on seen/unseen species trait R^2 and per-trait identifiability curves—appears unaddressed as a unified controlled experiment.

07.what_is_already_done: Multimodal citizen-science photo models already predict plant traits across species with weak supervision and reported cross-taxa generalisation, but none of the cited work quantifies within-species prediction variance versus between-species prior variance or runs an image-shuffle diagnostic to test whether images are actually used.
07.remaining_novel_angle: The prior-recall index plus within-species image-shuffle test as a diagnostic for prior-dominated trait prediction, and a prior-debiasing loss penalising prediction-species-mean correlation, appear unaddressed in the known core work and search hits.

10.what_is_already_done: Few-shot CNN adaptation has been applied to leaf trait segmentation and population-scale phenotyping in a single species (Populus trichocarpa), and few-shot meta-learning has been used for species range estimation, while PlantTraitNet already does multimodal trait inference from citizen-science photos.
10.remaining_novel_angle: The specific test of whether few-shot fine-tuning (5-20 photos) on unseen species improves functional-trait regression over zero-shot and whether gains scale with morphological distinctiveness rather than species frequency appears unaddressed.

12.what_is_already_done: Prior work uses citizen-science photos and ML to classify or map flower color (e.g., Convolvulus color polymorphism, HSV/k-means petal color pipelines) and to predict traits across taxa with CNNs, but does not systematically decompose color vs shape identifiability under seen-vs-unseen species splits.
12.remaining_novel_angle: The explicit seen-vs-unseen species evaluation isolating color identifiability from species-confounded shape/symmetry traits, plus a color-constancy augmentation ablation, is a distinct diagnostic framing not covered by the cited hits.
